policies.title: Tanzanian citizens: outside foreign-visitor visa regime
policies.summary: The Immigration Department's current entry guidance distinguishes Tanzanian citizens from foreign nationals subject to visa or visa-on-arrival procedures. The same-country ordinary-passport pair is therefore recorded as citizenship rather than a foreign visitor visa status.
conditions: All travellers must use designated formal entry points, appear to an immigration officer, complete the arrival declaration and produce a passport or other acceptable document.
This does not decide citizenship acquisition, dual nationality, passport validity, residence, customs, health, security, criminal process or individual border formalities.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: Tanzania visa-free visitors
policies.summary: The 2016 Visa Regulations' Third Schedule directly names 44 of this cohort as not requiring a visa. Current eVisa group guidance directly supports the two additional EAC/SADC entries (CD and ZW); the separate detailed eVisa-list URL was unavailable on re-review, so no wider unlisted complement is inferred.
conditions: This policy applies only to the directly supported ordinary-passport cohort. It does not establish a common stay limit, work entitlement, residence right, transit rule or special-document exemption.

The current eVisa guide's broad EAC/SADC/Commonwealth wording conflicts with its own detailed VOA/referral categories and with portions of the 2016 schedules. The current detailed visa-free endpoint returned a runtime error on re-review. The 44 statutory Third-Schedule codes are retained; CD and ZW are the only additional catalog codes directly supported by the current EAC/SADC wording and not contradicted by a current named route. Burundi and South Sudan remain unresolved because they are omitted from the statutory schedule and all current detailed categories despite the EAC prose.

All entry remains through designated points with a passport or other acceptable document, arrival declaration, and possible onward-travel, funds and current health/yellow-fever documentation. The Immigration Officer retains admission authority.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: Tanzania ordinary or multiple visa on arrival
policies.summary: The current official Immigration guideline expressly gives this named cohort both online and visa-on-arrival facilities. Because the same visitor visa can be issued at an official entry point, the easiest supported baseline is visa_on_arrival, not evisa.
conditions: The direct named schedule grants both online and on-arrival facilities. It does not make an online application mandatory, so this is not normalized as evisa. Issuance is only at an official designated entry point, not an assertion that every port offers an arrival visa.

An ordinary tourist visa is stated to cost USD 50 and be valid up to 90 days. United States passport holders visiting for tourism are instead required to use the USD 100 multiple visa, even for a single entry; the guide nevertheless includes the United States in the named on-arrival cohort.

The portal's raw lists overlap: Ghana, Saint Lucia and Saint Vincent are also on the live visa-free schedule, so their direct no-visa route prevails; Burkina Faso and Guinea appear in the raw VOA list but are referral cases, so the referral eVisa policy prevails. These codes are omitted from this VOA policy.

Ordinary visa holders may not work or conduct business. Transit, work, residence, business-only, diplomatic, official, service, refugee/stateless, special-document and Zanzibar-specific operating rules are not decided by this policy. Entry remains subject to documents, health, funds/onward travel and officer discretion.

application.label: Tanzania Immigration eVisa service
application.processingTime: The terms say online applications should be lodged ten days before expected travel; this does not apply where the visitor instead uses the expressly available on-arrival route.
steps: Choose either the official online visa application or the permitted visa-on-arrival procedure at an official entry point.
For an online application, submit the required documents and payment, then obtain the Visa Grant Notice through the portal before travel.
Present the required documents to Immigration. A grant notice or arrival-visa application does not guarantee admission.

policies.title: Referral ordinary passports: Tanzania advance electronic visa approval
policies.summary: Tanzania Immigration's current referral list prohibits this cohort from using visa on arrival without special Commissioner-General permission and requires an online application approved before travel. The online grant notice makes the ordinary baseline evisa.
conditions: Referral nationals must apply online and wait for approval before starting travel, unless they obtain special approval from the Commissioner General of Immigration. They are advised to apply at least two months before travel and supply local-host/contact and invitation or visa-application-letter information where available.

This policy is evisa because the official portal processes the online application and lets approved applicants download the Visa Grant Notice. It does not turn the exceptional Commissioner's permission into a nationality-wide VOA route.

The direct referral list takes precedence over the raw VOA schedule's Burkina Faso and Guinea entries. Refugee and stateless applicants also cannot use VOA but are document/status categories, not ordinary-passport nationality policies.

Ordinary visitor approval does not authorize work or business and remains subject to entry documents, designated ports, health/yellow-fever requirements, funds/onward evidence, security and immigration-officer discretion.

application.label: Tanzania Immigration referral visa application
application.processingTime: Referral applicants are advised to submit at least two months before travel and must wait for approval before commencing the journey.
steps: Submit the referral visa application through the official Tanzania Immigration portal.
Provide the passport, supporting documents, local-host details and an invitation or visa-application letter addressed to the Commissioner General where available.
Wait for approval, download the Visa Grant Notice from the portal, and present it with entry documents at a designated entry point.
